newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CBANK TELLS BIG BANKS TO HELP AGROBANKA.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CBANK TELLS BIG BANKS TO HELP AGROBANKA.

text.p: Czech National Bank Governor Josef Tosovsky on Tuesday said that the central bank had instructed the country's "big banks" to prepare up to six billion crowns to help the liquidity of Agrobanka a.s. .

"We have intiated for our big banks to have ready, if need be, liquidity of six billion crowns (for Agrobanka)," Tosovsky told a news conference called concerning the central bank's forced administration of Agrobanka, begun earlier on Tuesday.
Tosovsky did not elaborate on what form the liquidity help might take or from which source.

But the term "big banks" usually refers to the so-called "Big Four" Czech banks -- Ceska Sporitelna , Komercni Banka, Investicni a Postovni Banka and Ceskoslovensko Obchodni Banka a.s. (CSOB) -- all in which the state holds a significant state.
However, all but CSOB, have privately-held shares.

The CNB earlier on Tuesday put Agrobanka under "temporary forced administration" because of poor liquidity connected to the failure of Kreditni Banka a.s. in which Agrobanka and investors connected to both banks were heavily involved.

Tosovsky said problems at Agrobanka, the largest fully-private and fifth largest Czech bank overall, were connected "with liquidity and not solvency" and the CNB's intervention was taken as a precautionary step.

The CNB, in its measures announced on Tuesday, gave full guarantees to all depositors and creditors of Agrobanka, which had basic capital of four billion crowns as of the end of 1995, and said it would step in with it's own money if necessary.
Agrobanka is the 12th Czech bank in which the central bank has intervened in the post-Communist era, but the largest to date.
